skill.name: astrale-cli
skill.description: Command reference for connecting to Astrale Kernels, managing instances and identities, querying graphs, invoking callables, installing domains, and configuring UI projects.
skill.summary: Use documented Astrale CLI workflows for Kernel operations, authentication, graph data, diagnostics, and local UI tooling.
skill.author: astrale-os

security_audit.summary: All 269 static findings are documentation false positives, including Markdown delimiters, example URLs, and descriptions of owner-private credential caches. Token examples introduce one semantic risk by passing bearer credentials through command-line arguments. No evidence found of prompt injection, malicious exfiltration, or unauthorized execution; external CLI implementation was not included.

remediation.issue: Bearer token examples expose credentials through process arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer the selected identity or --as instead of --creds examples. Document process-list and tracing exposure; provide protected credential input if explicit tokens are required.

semantic_findings.title: Bearer Credentials Exposed Through Command Arguments
semantic_findings.description: The examples pass minted bearer credentials using --creds "$TOKEN" and --creds "$(astrale token --raw)". Shell expansion places credentials in process arguments, potentially exposing them to process inspection or execution logging while tokens remain valid.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly expand bearer credentials into argv. Exposure depends on local process visibility and logging; short token lifetimes reduce the exploitation window.

content.user_title: Manage Astrale Kernels with CLI Workflows
content.value_statement: Astrale operations require precise paths, identity selection, and command options. This reference guides assistants through Kernel operations, graph workflows, diagnostics, and local UI setup.
actual_capabilities: Guides instance selection, bookmarks, invitations, and authorized root identity recovery.
Explains canonical Kernel paths, node reads, schema introspection, and paginated graph queries.
Documents atomic graph mutations, callable input handling, dry runs, and binary output.
Explains domain installation, release verification, issuer consent, and uninstall modes.
Guides local UI initialization, component search, source installation, and project checks.
Documents identity selection, credential delegation, journal filtering, and authenticated browser sessions.
limitations: Provides documentation only; the Astrale CLI package and its implementation are not bundled.
Requires Node 22 or newer and authorized access to existing Kernels for remote operations.
Does not build, deploy, or publish domains; those workflows belong to the separate astrale-domain binary.
Managed instance operations require a configured Admin Domain; permissions can limit inventory and query results.

use_cases.title: Inspect Application Graph Data
use_cases.description: Read nodes, inspect callable schemas, and paginate bounded graph queries on an explicitly selected instance.

use_cases.title: Plan Domain Updates
use_cases.description: Review installed releases, dependency compatibility, and issuer changes before approving a grouped domain installation.

use_cases.title: Configure Local UI Projects
use_cases.description: Initialize React and Tailwind CSS projects, search available patterns, and review source changes before adding components.

prompt_templates.title: Check Connection and Identity
prompt_templates.prompt: Use astrale-cli to explain read-only connection and identity checks for staging. Do not print tokens or change configuration.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Paginated Graph Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a bounded query for /:notes.example:class.Note on staging using identity reader. Explain cursor pagination without running mutations.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Mutation Before Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Review mutation.v3.json and prepare an Astrale mutation dry run. Explain preconditions and atomicity; require approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Authorized Domain Upgrade
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a grouped domain upgrade on staging. Review release pins, compatibility, and issuer consent using an authorized identity; require approval before installation.

output_examples.input: Explain how to read notes from staging without changing data.
output: Select staging explicitly and use an identity authorized to read notes.
Query the Note class with a finite limit and structured output.
Resume with each returned cursor until no continuation remains.

output_examples.input: Explain how to review a mutation before sending it.
output: Use mutation dry mode to admit and display the canonical document without connecting to a Kernel.
Review the operations and preconditions against the intended instance.
Require approval before executing the atomic transition.

output_examples.input: Explain how to protect locally edited Astrale UI components.
output: Ordinary component addition refuses to replace locally edited installed files.
Preview proposed changes with dry-run mode.
Use overwrite and confirmation flags only after reviewing the intended replacement.

best_practices: Select the instance and least-privileged identity explicitly, and verify current command help before remote operations.
Review dry runs and release pins; approve mutations, issuer changes, root recovery, and destructive uninstalls explicitly.
Prefer identity selection over bearer arguments; keep secret payloads in protected files or stdin, and redact shared diagnostics.
anti_patterns: Relying on an ambient active instance or root identity for unattended production changes.
Placing bearer credentials or secret payloads in command arguments, logs, or issue reports.
Treating partial domain inventory or authorization-masked reads as proof that data is missing.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides an Astrale CLI reference for assistants. It does not include the CLI binary or verify its implementation.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Executing commands also requires a local CLI installation and authorized credentials.

faq.question: Can it deploy domains?
faq.answer: No. The CLI connects to existing Kernels and installs published releases. Building, deploying, and publishing use the separate astrale-domain binary.

faq.question: Can I inspect changes without applying them?
faq.answer: Mutations support --dry, while calls and UI additions support --dry-run. These previews do not replace permission checks during execution.

faq.question: How should I handle credentials?
faq.answer: Prefer identity selection. Bearer arguments can expose tokens; use protected files or stdin for secret call payloads and avoid logging credentials.

faq.question: Why is a domain absent from the installed list?
faq.answer: The list omits built-in, local, and unreadable domains. An absent origin does not prove that the domain is not installed.
